title: The Yakut ancestors north along the Lena, c. AD 1200–1600
summary: The Yakut (Sakha) speak a Turkic language and herd horses and cattle in the coldest inhabited basin on earth, around the Lena. Their ancestors came there from the Baikal country, at a time put anywhere from the first millennium AD to the sixteenth century, going down the Lena into land held by the Evenki and Yukaghir. The dates and the numbers who moved are argued.

legs.source: Yakuts (Wikipedia): north along the Lena from the Baikal region
legs.doubt: Accounts put the Yakut arrival on the middle Lena anywhere from the first millennium to the sixteenth century; the genetic evidence and the Russian records disagree on how large the movement was.

events.label: Lake Baikal country
events.text: The Yakut language's nearest relatives are Turkic languages of southern Siberia, which is why the Baikal and upper Lena are named as where they lived before.

events.label: The Yakutsk basin
events.text: By the time Russians arrived in the 1620s the Yakut were the main people of the middle Lena. Yakutsk was founded there as a fort in 1632.
